source: R&S Injury Law – Deaths in Yosemite National Park (2023-05-02, updated 2025-07-31)
notes: ~900 documented deaths studied 1857–2023. Percentages represent share of total deaths by cause.

fall.description: Falls from cliffs, waterfalls, and steep terrain

vehicle.description: Motor vehicle accidents on park roads and parking areas

drowning.description: Drowning in rivers, waterfalls, and pools

medical.description: Heart attacks, illness, and other medical emergencies

rockfall.description: Rockfall and landslides striking hikers or campers

search_rescue.description: Exposure, hypothermia, and overdue hiker recoveries

lightning.description: Lightning strikes on exposed terrain and summits

fire_related.description: Wildfire, smoke inhalation, and burn injuries

high_risk_locations.name: Half Dome Cables
risk_factors: 80-degree granite cable climb
severe lightning exposure on summit dome
extreme crowding during permit season
altitude 2693 m — hypoxia risk
high_risk_locations.notes: Most deaths occur on the cables or the sub-dome approach. Lightning fatalities spike July–August afternoon storms.

high_risk_locations.name: Mist Trail – Vernal Falls Footbridge Area
risk_factors: Spray-polished granite steps become glass-slick
Hikers cross barriers to stand near the lip
Spring snowmelt creates fast, deep approach channels
Guardrail gaps near Emerald Pool
high_risk_locations.notes: Several deaths from slipping on wet rock and being carried over the 97 m falls.

high_risk_locations.name: Nevada Falls – Approach and Lip
risk_factors: Strong current above falls deceives swimmers
Polished granite provides no grip if swept
173 m drop — unsurvivable
Warning signs frequently ignored
high_risk_locations.notes: Multiple drowning deaths from swimmers ignoring closure signs and entering the river above the falls.

high_risk_locations.name: El Capitan Base and Rockfall Zone
risk_factors: 3000-foot granite face sheds exfoliation slabs seasonally
Climbers exposed during multi-day ascents
Valley floor spectators struck by debris
September 2017: 100-tonne slab release killed 1
high_risk_locations.notes: Rockfall risk year-round but highest in spring (freeze-thaw) and autumn. El Cap Meadow is a documented impact zone.

high_risk_locations.name: Merced River – Valley Floor Crossings
risk_factors: Cold snowmelt water causes rapid incapacitation
Deceptively calm surface over fast sub-surface currents
Underwater rocks and log debris
Non-swimmers and children entering without PFDs
high_risk_locations.notes: Most drownings occur at popular swimming holes like Sentinel Beach and Cathedral Beach during peak flow.

high_risk_locations.name: Yosemite Valley Loop Road
risk_factors: High tourist traffic volume – millions of cars per year
Cyclists and pedestrians share narrow roadway
Wildlife (bears, deer) cross unpredictably
Night driving with limited lighting
high_risk_locations.notes: Vehicle fatalities distributed across the valley one-way loop, including tunnel and Southside Drive.

high_risk_locations.name: Tioga Road / CA-120 (High Country)
risk_factors: High speed limit on mountain curves
Ice and snow during shoulder seasons
Sudden weather whiteouts above 3000 m
Deer and bear crossings dawn/dusk
high_risk_locations.notes: Road open approximately May–November. Most crashes occur on curves between Crane Flat and Tioga Pass.

high_risk_locations.name: Yosemite Falls Trail – Upper Section
risk_factors: Exposed rocky ridgeline with sheer drops to valley
Switchback trail deteriorates in wet conditions
Off-trail scrambling near the falls lip
Rescue helicopter access difficult in this drainage
high_risk_locations.notes: Multiple deaths from falls near the upper falls viewing area. One notable 1999 case involved off-trail exploration.

high_risk_locations.name: Clouds Rest Ridge
risk_factors: Highest exposed ridgeline in Yosemite (2985 m)
Afternoon convective storms July–August
No shelter within 1 km of summit
Steep 1000 m drop on north face
high_risk_locations.notes: Multiple lightning fatalities during afternoon storms. Park service issues regular storm advisories for this ridge.

high_risk_locations.name: Tuolumne Meadows – High Country Trailheads
risk_factors: 2621 m altitude – altitude sickness for unprepared hikers
Late and early season snow cover obscures trails
Remote drainages with multi-day rescue lead times
Temperature drops below 0°C even in July nights
high_risk_locations.notes: Most deaths involve lost or overdue hikers in the backcountry who succumb to exposure. John Muir Trail junctions.

high_risk_locations.name: Glacier Point Road – Overlooks
risk_factors: Narrow two-lane road with switchbacks to 2200 m
Pullout areas immediately adjacent to cliff edges
Ice in spring and autumn
Tourist photo stops near unguarded edges
high_risk_locations.notes: Deaths from both vehicle accidents and falls from overlook viewpoints.

high_risk_locations.name: Cathedral Lakes – Subalpine Zone
risk_factors: Open subalpine terrain with no lightning shelter
Popular day-hike destination during storm season
2900 m elevation, exposed granite slabs
Afternoon storm onset within 20 min typical
high_risk_locations.notes: Several lightning deaths on the granite slabs en route to and at the lakes.

high_risk_locations.name: Bridalveil Fall – Base Pool
risk_factors: Slippery rocks surrounding plunge pool
Strong wind gusts (100+ km/h recorded) below the falls
Overcrowding on limited viewing platform
Pool depth unpredictable in spring
high_risk_locations.notes: Visitors attempting to approach the base slip on wet granite. Wind can push people off balance.

high_risk_locations.name: Hetch Hetchy Reservoir
risk_factors: Cold deep reservoir with steep canyon walls
Limited rescue access – no road to water's edge
Remote – response times exceed 45 min
Swimming prohibited but violations common
high_risk_locations.notes: Drowning deaths from illegal swimming. Canyon walls prevent self-rescue.

high_risk_locations.name: Mirror Lake / Tenaya Creek
risk_factors: Creek floods dramatically in spring snowmelt
Flat trail lures hikers close to fast water
Children frequently near water unsupervised
Footbridge washed out periodically
high_risk_locations.notes: Spring flood events have swept hikers off the trail. Seasonal closure signs often ignored.
